articles.headline: Week 3 NFL highlights: Best plays, moments, touchdowns, more
articles.description: Sunday of Week 3 has seen 13 games played, with Lamar Jackson, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam Darnold having big stat days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continued Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, Jaylen Warren had a career outing in the Pittsburgh Steelers' win against AFC North rival Cincinnati Bengals, Jameis Winston stepped in to lead the New York Giants to a victory over the Tennessee Titans and the Washington Commanders slipped by the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Among the highlights from the afternoon slate of four games, the Baltimore Ravens stunned the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro on a Tyler Loop 56-yard field goal and the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after beating the Saints in New Orleans.

The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day, so keep checking here for "Sunday Night Football" highlights.

Week 3 highlights

articles.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
articles.description: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. On the flip side, fantasy stars Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown had disappointing games.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the third week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 3

1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

He's sure proving worthy of that No. 1 overall pick. He has scored at least 23 fantasy points in all three games, posted 75% snap and 78% rushing shares, and he has totaled an easily position-best 98.3 points for the season. That latter number ranks 15th in history through three team games of any season. Isiah Pacheco's back and MCL injuries have locked Gibbs in as a three-down dynamo, and the odds are good that he will maintain his positional lead in fantasy points for the duration of 2026. -- Cockcroft

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, and Sam Darnold, QB, Seattle Seahawks

It's incredible to think that Smith-Njigba is off to the stellar start that he is despite Darnold having missed nearly all of the first two weeks due to injury and the team's running game having been only so-so thus far. Smith-Njigba scored 35.36 fantasy points, giving him 104.06 through three games, the fourth most ever through that many by any player. Meanwhile, Darnold threw a pair of interceptions in his return to the lineup, but he didn't seem at all slowed by the glute injury, finishing with 27.66 points of his own. Smith-Njigba's elite play should bring Darnold's fantasy utility up, and the two have a good matchup against the struggling Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4 before hitting a tougher stretch of the 2026 schedule (SF, @DEN, KC in Weeks 5-7). -- Cockcroft

3. Joe Burrow, QB, and Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

In the Week 3 loss to the Steelers, Burrow notched his best numbers of the season, completing 75.7% of his throws for 282 yards and three touchdowns, plus he rushed for 13 yards (22.58 points). Chase caught nine of a team-high 12 targets for 98 yards and a score (24.8 points). That gives Chase two straight games of 24 or more points after that rough opening week. Chase will remain a top-three play at wide receiver for Week 4, while Burrow -- who has thrown for at least two touchdowns in back-to-back games -- will be a lower-tier QB1 in my ranks. -- Bowen

4. Geno Smith, QB, Garrett Wilson, WR, and Kenyon Sadiq, TE, New York Jets

In a positive matchup versus the Detroit secondary, Smith scored a season-best 26.04 points, throwing for 321 yards and four touchdowns. Wilson caught 10 of a team-high 13 targets, finishing with 107 yards and a touchdown (26.7 points), plus Sadiq posted his first breakout game, bringing in seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score (23.5 points). articles.headline: Kirk Cousins passes for 3 TDs and the unbeaten Raiders come back to top the Saints 35-27
articles.description: — Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns, and the Las Vegas Raiders overcame an 11-point second-half deficit to beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday and remain unbeaten under rookie coach Klint Kubiak.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns, and the Las Vegas Raiders overcame an 11-point second-half deficit to beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday and remain unbeaten under rookie coach Klint Kubiak.


              The game shifted on a play that will be seen as controversial and unjust by some — and certainly Saints fans.


              The series that led to the Raiders' go-ahead score began when Las Vegas defensive end Malcolm Koonce sacked Tyler Shough as the Saints QB started his throwing motion.


              The ball went backward and was ruled a fumble that was recovered by the Raiders — a different ruling than was made after a similar play involving the Saints in Week 1 at Detroit. On that play, an apparent New Orleans strip-sack of the Lions' Jared Goff was ruled incomplete on video review after the Saints thought they had recovered a fumble for a touchdown.


              The Superdome crowd booed as officials, following a video review, upheld the call that the play had resulted in a turnover on the New Orleans 45.


              Six plays later, Cousins connected with Cody White for a 4-yard touchdown to make it 28-27.


              Cousins gave Las Vegas (3-0) an eight-point lead with a 4-yard TD pass to Brock Bowers. The Saints (1-2) got the ball twice more with a chance to tie it, but one drive stalled on fourth down and another on Juwan Johnson's fumble with 1:02 left.


              Shough passed for 255 yards and a career-high four touchdowns — including two to Johnson. Shough's other scoring passes went to Noah Fant from short range. But the second-year QB also turned the ball over twice, first on his fumble and later on an interception that set up the Raiders' final scoring drive.


              Bowers, making his season debut after coming back from a knee injury during training camp, caught 10 passes for 116 yards and his short TD. Mike Washington ignited the Raiders' comeback with a tackle-breaking 36-yard scoring run that cut New Orleans' lead to 27-22 in the third quarter. Matt Gay kicked three field goals for Las Vegas, which also failed on a pair of 2-point conversions after second-half TDs.


              New Orleans' Chris Olave caught nine passes for 107 yards, his second 100-yard game this season.


              Injuries
              Raiders: WR Jack Bech left the game with a forearm injury.


              Saints: LB Pete Warner left in the first half with a neck and shoulder injury (stinger). ... RB Travis Etienne left with an apparent hamstring pull. Edge rusher Anfernee Jennings left with a knee injury.


              Up next
              Raiders: Host Kansas City next Sunday.


              Saints: Host Atlanta on Monday, Oct. 5.


              ----

articles.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
articles.description: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「自分には関係ない」元マンC監督のマンチーニ氏、有罪報道を一蹴
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・マンチーニ氏は、自身が指揮を執っていた期間に犯したとされる財務違反について、古巣のマンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグから有罪と認定されたとする報道を一蹴しました。
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm. 

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
